newsitem.title: VATICAN: Netanyahu re-invites Pope to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu re-invites Pope to Israel.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday renewed a standing government invitation for Pope John Paul to visit Israel.
"We look forward to receiving you in Jerusalem," Netanyahu told the Pope as he was leaving the Pontiff's study after a 20-minute private audience.
No date for an eventual visit was given but a Vatican statement said Netanyahu had invited the Pope to make a visit "as soon as possible".

In 1994, the Pope accepted an open invitation made by the late prime minister Yitzhak Rabin to visit the Holy Land. A diplomatic source said a papal trip to Israel had been on the agenda of the meeting between the Pope and Netanyahu.

The Pope, who has often said he wants to visit Holy Land sites by the year 2000, last year accepted an invitation by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to visit Christ's birth place in Bethlehem at the turn of the millennium.
Netanyahu, on an official visit to Italy, was to meet Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini later on Monday.
